cohort.definition: Undergraduates and recent graduates entering McKinsey's client-facing consulting track as Business Analysts (and Sophomore Summer Business Analyst interns). Expert and internal tracks are separate cohorts.
cohort.level: entry-level: Business Analyst and sophomore summer intern
cohort.time_window: process as described on the firm's careers and interview-preparation pages, checked October 2026

compensation_notes.statement: The firm publishes no analyst pay figure on the careers sources checked for this record. Compensation for Business Analysts circulates through press and community reporting; it is labeled anecdotal wherever this product mentions it, and no figure is stated here.

data_sources.label: McKinsey official careers blog: global recruiting update — application review, the Problem Solving Game, and the qualities interviews test
McKinsey official careers page (internal roles): the four qualities the firm says it interviews for, and recruiter-provided practice material
McKinsey official interview-preparation page (archived copy of mckinsey.com/careers/interviewing): practice cases and the Solve gamified assessment

entry_routes.accessibility_note: The standard door: application, the Solve assessment, then interviews pairing a case with a personal-experience conversation. Practice cases are officially published — use them.
entry_routes.route: Business Analyst application (full-time, final-year and recent graduates)

entry_routes.accessibility_note: An earlier look at the same screens for sophomores; a realistic target for students who start case practice a year ahead of the full-time cycle.
Adjacent doors with different day jobs: QuantumBlack / tech and data roles interview on overlapping qualities with technical cases added.
entry_routes.route: Adjacent practices and internal roles (data, tech, design) as a parallel application

hiring_bar_summary.statement: McKinsey states the qualities it interviews for — personal impact, entrepreneurial drive, inclusive leadership and courageous change — alongside problem-solving skill, and it screens applications before inviting candidates to its gamified problem-solving assessment. The firm publishes no GPA cutoff or school list on the sources checked; school and GPA screens students describe are community-reported, and this record labels them that way.

hiring_cadence.statement: Consulting recruiting runs on campus-cycle timing — applications cluster in the fall for the following summer's internships and for full-time starts — but the exact deadlines are office- and school-specific and set each cycle. The firm's careers site for your office and graduation year is the only reliable date source; this record intentionally states no deadline it could not verify.

interview_styles.statement: Case interviews: interviewer-led business problems with published practice cases (the firm posts full sample cases with recommended answers for preparation).

Solve: a gamified assessment of intrinsic problem-solving skills, for which the firm says no preparation is required or expected; depending on role, candidates may instead or also take an assessment test on job-related abilities.

Personal Experience Interview: one experience explored in depth against the firm's stated qualities — candidates' own accounts describe using structured story frameworks (situation, task, action, result, lessons) to prepare.

known_biases_of_data: No population sample exists for this record: McKinsey publishes its process and its stated qualities, not the composition of who passes. School and GPA patterns in circulation are community-reported and are not restated here as facts.
The firm's own recruiting blog is a marketing surface written to encourage applications; its warmth about support and coaching is the firm's account of itself.
Process details vary by office and role; the archived interview-preparation page is an older official snapshot and is labeled with its archive source.

entries.label: All majors — no major requirement published
entries.note: The firm's stated screens are qualities and problem-solving, not a degree subject; this record states no major mix because none is published in the sources checked.

path_patterns.pattern: Application reviewed, then the Problem Solving Game (Solve), then interviews — the sequence the firm's own recruiting update describes
Sophomore summer internship first, converting into the full-time Business Analyst pool a cycle later

entries.label: No feeder-employer pattern published
entries.note: For an undergraduate cohort the relevant 'feeders' are internships and leadership roles, and the firm publishes no distribution of them; this record states none rather than inventing one.

process_stages.description: Apply on the careers site; per the firm's recruiting update, your CV is reviewed by a recruiter before any assessment invite.
Invited candidates take Solve, the firm's gamified assessment of intrinsic problem-solving skills; the firm states no preparation is required or expected for the game itself.

Interviews test the four stated qualities plus problem solving, combining a case discussion with a personal-experience conversation; the firm publishes practice cases and recruiters share preparation material.

red_flags.statement: Solve is designed so that preparation is neither required nor expected — candidates sold expensive 'Solve hacks' are buying something the firm's own page undercuts.
The personal-experience part goes deep on one story; candidates whose examples are inflated tend to be found out by follow-up questions — prepare real experiences in depth instead.

referral_weight_notes.statement: The published process is an open application with recruiter review and a standardized assessment — no referral track is described on the sources checked. Networking's documented value here is information (what the interviews test, office realities), not a screen bypass.

entries.label: No school distribution published
entries.note: McKinsey recruits on many campuses and publishes no school mix for analyst classes in the sources checked. Community claims about target schools are folklore until measured; this record states no share.

revealed.statement: Revealed by the process design itself: a standardized gamified assessment sits between the CV and human interviews, so raw problem-solving under novel conditions is screened before polish and pedigree get their full hearing.
Revealed by the personal-experience format: one story, probed for detail — depth and ownership of a real experience beat a long list of shallow leadership titles.

stated.statement: Interviews focus on technical and problem-solving skills and experience, plus four qualities the firm names for future hires: personal impact, entrepreneurial drive, inclusive leadership and courageous change.
The firm's recruiting update says interviews look for inclusive leadership, personal impact, entrepreneurial drive and problem-solving skills.

entries.label: Structured problem solving (case craft)
entries.note: The firm publishes full practice cases with recommended answers — the clearest public signal of the skill the case interview tests.

entries.label: Quantified-impact storytelling
entries.note: From the firm's stated qualities and candidates' preparation accounts: experiences told with specific actions and measurable results, structured so follow-ups have somewhere real to go.

thesis_text: McKinsey's screens are unusually public: an application and recruiter CV review, the Solve gamified assessment, then interviews that pair a case with a deep personal-experience conversation against four stated qualities — personal impact, entrepreneurial drive, inclusive leadership and courageous change. The design tells you the revealed preference: standardized problem-solving is tested before pedigree gets a full hearing, and one real story in depth beats a decorated resume. What this record cannot tell you is who actually gets in by school or GPA — the firm publishes none of it, and community numbers are labeled folklore here, not facts.

values_culture_signals.statement: The qualities the firm names — personal impact, entrepreneurial drive, inclusive leadership, courageous change — are its culture screen stated in its own words; recruiters are described as guiding candidates with practice cases and problem-solving tests.

schema_normalized: 2026-10-12 integration: envelope mapped to the 125-career-intel validator schema (cohort object, data_sources label/url, dist basis). No facts added, removed, or altered.
